note: Maintained daily. Every item links to the page that confirms it.

happened.title: Supreme Court refuses DOJ's bid to set aside about 20,000 California mail ballots; Boasberg rejects Democrats' suit over voter-roll pressure
happened.what: In an unsigned one-line order with no noted dissents, the Supreme Court denied the administration's emergency request to make California segregate about 20,000 mail ballots from alleged noncitizens; the same evening Judge Boasberg denied Democratic groups' request to block DOJ from pressing election officials to remove alleged noncitizens, finding they lacked standing, and a 9th Circuit panel paused an order restricting DOJ contact with election workers.
happened.why: The disputed ballots are counted in California's competitive House seats, and the rulings close the last pre-election court fights over who is counted.

happened.title: Final ratings: Sabato's Crystal Ball calls 53 Senate seats, 239 House seats and 28 governors at least Lean D; Cook moves Michigan to Lean D and leaves six Senate toss-ups
happened.what: Kondik and Coleman's final ratings have no Senate toss-ups (53 at least Lean D, 47 at least Lean R), 239-196 in the House after the last toss-ups broke 14-3 to Lean D, and 28-22 among governors, moving Georgia and Nevada to Lean D, Alaska to Likely D and New Hampshire to Lean R; Cook's final Senate ratings move Michigan from Toss Up to Lean D and keep Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Ohio and Texas as toss-ups.
happened.why: Both raters now have Democrats favored for the Senate as well as the House, with Iowa the one Senate race Sabato gives Republicans an edge in among the closest contests.
happened.src: Sabato's Crystal Ball (Kyle Kondik and J. Miles Coleman), Nov 2; FiftyPlusOne (Cook's Nov 2 map), Nov 3

happened.title: Election-eve polls: AtlasIntel has Democrats ahead in every Senate race it polled; Emerson has Collins +2, Husted +2 and Abbott +1; Rasmussen has Ohio tied and Hinson +1
happened.what: On RealClearPolling's Nov 2 list, AtlasIntel shows Talarico +6, El-Sayed +8, Jackson +9, Brown +7, Hamilton +7, Turek +5, Peltola +5 and Flanagan +2; Emerson's final polls show Collins 51-49, Husted 48-46, Abbott 50-49, Talarico +2 and El-Sayed +6; Rasmussen's Oct 27-31 polls have Brown and Husted tied 46-46, Jackson +3 in Maine, Hinson +1 in Iowa, Sand +5 and Acton +4; the Times/Siena finals released Nov 1 have Democrats ahead in Michigan, Texas, Maine, Ohio and Kansas, Iowa within a point.
happened.why: The closing polls agree on a Democratic Senate map but disagree by several points in Ohio, Maine, Texas and Iowa, the races that decide how large the majority is.
happened.src: RealClearPolling latest polls, Nov 2; Rasmussen Reports, Nov 2
happened.aff: Rasmussen Reports is R-aligned in ElectIndex's ratings

happened.title: Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers for Senate two days before the election; Schumer calls it 'a despicable betrayal'
happened.what: Rep. Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost August's Democratic Senate primary, endorsed Mike Rogers after a Detroit church service with him: 'Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away... And he's right. And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.' Her chief of staff resigned; Michigan Democratic chair Curtis Hertel said she 'is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future'; Abdul El-Sayed said 'None of this matters'; Trump praised her on Truth Social. More than 1.8 million Michiganders had already voted as of Friday.
happened.why: Michigan is the Democrats' most exposed open Senate seat, and a sitting Democratic congresswoman's defection is the biggest late shock in any Senate race.
happened.src: AP (Joey Cappelletti, Corey Williams and Mike Householder) via PBS NewsHour, Nov 1

happened.title: Judge Gleason dismisses DOJ's Alaska suit seeking to block certification over the second 'Dan Sullivan'
happened.what: U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the Justice Department's Oct 22 lawsuit, which sought to bar certification of any result affected by voter confusion between Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and the unaffiliated Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., finding DOJ offered 'no workable plan as to how it proposes to segregate ballots' or protect ballot secrecy. U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman said the FBI and his office added resources to a criminal probe, and FBI agents visited at least two Daniel J. Sullivan donors in Sitka and Petersburg.
happened.why: The ruling removes the main legal path to delaying an Alaska Senate result that could decide the majority, though the criminal probe and a possible appeal continue.

happened.title: Final Times/Siena polls: Democrats lead in Michigan, Texas, Maine, Ohio and Kansas, narrowly in Alaska; Iowa tied
happened.what: The New York Times/Siena likely-voter polls (Oct 23-Nov 1): El-Sayed 53-42 in Michigan, Talarico 50-43 in Texas, Jackson 51-45 in Maine, Brown 49-44 in Ohio, Hamilton 49-44 in Kansas (Graham 4), Peltola 48-46 in Alaska, Turek 48-47 in Iowa; governors: Benson 52-39, Hinojosa 48-47 over Abbott, Pingree 49-37 (Bennett 8), Acton 49-43, Holscher 48-47, Kreiss-Tomkins 54-46 after ranked-choice transfers, Sand 51-43. Samples 610 (Alaska) to 1,215 (Texas); margins of error 3.4 to 5.0 points.
happened.why: The last major battery before Election Day puts Democrats ahead or even in every Republican-held Senate target the polls can reach, including Texas and Iowa.
happened.src: Siena Research Institute, Nov 1; Newsweek (Hugh Cameron), Nov 2

happened.title: Silver Bulletin puts Democrats at 80.1% for the Senate; Silver says the polls point to 'a really big year for Democrats' but warns of another systematic error
happened.what: Nate Silver's Nov 1 post gave Democrats an 80.1% chance of Senate control, calling the Times/Siena results 'fantastic numbers for Democrats' and saying Republicans 'are in for a long night on Tuesday' if Democrats come home in blue states and Republicans don't in red ones, 'two very, very big ifs'; he warned of 'another embarrassing systematic polling error.' RacetotheWH projects 53 Democratic seats (79.4%). AtlasIntel's national poll (Oct 28-Nov 1, 3,566 adults) has the generic ballot 55.5-41.4.
happened.why: The forecasters have converged near four-in-five odds of a Democratic Senate going into Election Day.
happened.src: Newsweek (Hugh Cameron), Nov 2; Silver Bulletin, Nov 1

happened.title: Inside Elections' final ratings move 63 races toward Democrats, project a 20-30 seat House gain and 4-6 Senate seats
happened.what: Nathan Gonzales made 64 changes (45 House, 9 Senate, 10 governor), all but Oregon's governor race toward Democrats: Senate Georgia to Likely D, Ohio and Texas to Tilt D, Iowa and Kansas to Toss-up, Nebraska and South Carolina to Tilt R, Louisiana and Mississippi to Likely R; governors Alaska, Georgia, Ohio and Wisconsin to Tilt D, Nevada to Toss-up, Texas to Tilt R; House moves include CO-05, FL-22, KY-06, MI-04, MT-01, PA-01 and TX-35 to Toss-up and AZ-06, CO-08, FL-14, FL-25, NC-01, NC-11, OH-07, OH-09, PA-10, TX-15, VA-02 and WI-03 to Tilt D. 'Democrats appear well on their way to winning the House majority.'
happened.why: The most bullish Inside Elections projection of the cycle puts the Democratic House range above the app's seat count and makes the Senate a Democratic pickup of four to six.

happened.title: 9th Circuit refuses DOJ's bid to set aside about 20,000 California mail ballots; DOJ says it will go to the Supreme Court
happened.what: A 2-1 panel (Judges Mark Bennett and Gabriel Sanchez, Patrick Bumatay dissenting) found no clear error in the district court's finding that 'there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals.' Separately, Judge Trina Thompson barred DOJ from threatening election workers or demanding ballots be segregated, another panel put federal noncitizen-voting investigations in nine states on hold until after Election Day, and at least three Los Angeles County election officials were subpoenaed to a grand jury for Nov 4.
happened.why: The rulings keep California's full count in place for its competitive House seats while the Justice Department's challenges move to after the election.

happened.title: Trump revives his Dubuque and Salina rallies a day after canceling them, then holds both Sunday
happened.what: After the RNC canceled the Saturday Salina and Sunday Dubuque rallies Thursday night in favor of tele-rallies in nearly 20 states, both were back on by Friday morning, moved to Sunday Nov 1: Dubuque at Five Flags Center at 2 p.m. and Salina Regional Airport at 6 p.m. Trump spoke about two hours in Dubuque and about 90 minutes in Salina, where Sen. Roger Marshall spoke and Trump said 'This is our last stop. We're closing it down tonight'; AP counted more than two dozen Trump rallies in 19 states since Oct 1.
happened.why: Iowa and Kansas are the two Republican-held Senate seats the final polls call even, and the reversal put the president in both on the last day of early voting.
happened.src: AP via KCRG, Oct 30; AP via KCTV5, Nov 1

happened.title: Cook moves Nebraska to Lean R and Florida to Likely R, shifts 12 House seats toward Democrats, projects a 12-25 seat gain
happened.what: Cook Political Report's Jessica Taylor and Erin Covey moved the Nebraska Senate race from Likely to Lean Republican and Florida's from Solid to Likely Republican, and made 'twelve new House race rating changes, all in the direction of Democrats' (PA-08 and OH-09 to Lean D; CO-05, PA-01 and SC-01 to Toss Up; FL-07, FL-09 and IN-05 to Lean R; NC-05, NC-09, NJ-02 and WA-05 to Likely R), projecting that Democrats 'flip 12 to 25 seats, giving them as many as 240 seats' if they win all 18 Toss Ups, and calling Democrats 'the slight favorites' for the Senate with seven races inside the margin of error.
happened.why: The last Cook House update before Election Day puts the Democratic range at or above the model's seat count, and Nebraska's move adds a seventh Republican-held Senate seat the raters see in play.
happened.src: Cook Political Report (Jessica Taylor and Erin Covey), Oct 30; Newsweek (Joe Edwards), Oct 30; Political Wire, Oct 30

happened.title: Emerson has Hamilton +4 in Kansas and Masterson +4 for governor; Post/Schar has Hamilton +10; co/efficient has Hinson +2 in Iowa; Quantus has Paxton +1 in Texas
happened.what: Emerson College's Kansas poll (Oct 26-28, 800 likely voters) has Adam Hamilton 49-45 over Sen. Roger Marshall (50-47 with leaners) and Ty Masterson 50-46 over Cindy Holscher for governor, while The Washington Post/George Mason Schar School poll has Hamilton 54-44 and Holscher 51-45; co/efficient's Iowa poll (Oct 28, 1,020 likely voters) has Ashley Hinson 48-46 over Josh Turek and Rob Sand 50-45 over Zach Lahn; Quantus Insights (Oct 26-28, 1,221 likely voters) has Ken Paxton 49-48 over James Talarico and Gov. Greg Abbott 52-46, and Texas Southern University's poll (Oct 21-25, 2,000 likely voters) has Talarico 49-47 and Abbott 50-47.
happened.why: Kansas, Iowa and Texas are the three Republican-held Senate seats the markets price closest to even, and the final-week polls keep all three inside the margin of error.
happened.src: Emerson College Polling, Oct 30; co/efficient, Oct 29; RealClearPolling latest polls, Oct 30; San Angelo LIVE (TSU poll), Oct 29
happened.aff: co/efficient and Quantus Insights are Republican-leaning pollsters

upcoming.title: Nevada polls close; Alaska follows after midnight ET
upcoming.what: Polls close at 10 p.m. ET in Nevada and Montana; most of Alaska closes at midnight ET and the Aleutian Islands at 1 a.m. ET on Nov. 4.
upcoming.why: Alaska's Senate race, rated a Toss-up by Inside Elections, is likely to be among the last competitive contests to report.

upcoming.title: First polls close in Indiana and Kentucky
upcoming.what: Polls in the Eastern time portions of Indiana and Kentucky close at 6 p.m. ET, with the rest of both states closing at 7 p.m. ET.
upcoming.why: The first returns of the night include House races such as KY-06, which Inside Elections moved to Lean Republican.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Georgia, South Carolina, Virginia, most of Florida
upcoming.what: Polls close at 7 p.m. ET in Georgia, South Carolina, Virginia and Vermont, in most of Florida (the western Panhandle at 8 p.m. ET) and at most New Hampshire polling places (all by 8 p.m. ET).
upcoming.why: First returns arrive in the Georgia, South Carolina, Florida and New Hampshire Senate races and the Georgia and Florida governor races.

upcoming.title: Mail-ballot deadlines: Florida 7 p.m., Pennsylvania 8 p.m.
upcoming.what: Florida mail ballots must reach supervisors by 7 p.m. and Pennsylvania's county offices by 8 p.m.; Pennsylvania cannot start counting mail ballots until Election Day.
upcoming.why: Florida's outstanding mail leans Democratic and Pennsylvania had about 235,000 approved mail ballots unreturned, so late arrivals shape the first counts in both states' House races.
upcoming.src: WFLA via Yahoo, Nov 2; Pennsylvania Department of State mail-ballot report, Nov 2

upcoming.title: Polls close in North Carolina and Ohio
upcoming.what: Polls close at 7:30 p.m. ET in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia.
upcoming.why: Results begin in the North Carolina and Ohio Senate races and the Ohio governor race.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Maine, Pennsylvania, most of Michigan, Texas
upcoming.what: Polls close at 8 p.m. ET in Maine, Pennsylvania and the rest of New Hampshire, and in most of Michigan, Texas and Kansas, whose westernmost areas close at 9 p.m. ET.
upcoming.why: First results arrive in the Maine, Michigan, Texas and Kansas Senate races and the Michigan and Texas governor races.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Arizona
upcoming.what: Polls close at 9 p.m. ET in Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin and Arizona.
upcoming.why: Results begin in the Iowa, Minnesota and Nebraska Senate races and the Iowa, Wisconsin and Arizona governor races.

upcoming.title: Los Angeles County election officials before a federal grand jury
upcoming.what: At least three Los Angeles County election officials were subpoenaed to appear before a federal grand jury the day after the election, as the Justice Department pursues its noncitizen-voting claims after the 9th Circuit refused to segregate about 20,000 ballots.
upcoming.why: The dispute over California ballots could shape challenges to close House counts in the state after Election Day.
